company_notes:
Summary: PixelForge builds an IDE copilot embedded in VS Code and a custom web editor for enterprise customers. Primary aim: extremely low-latency streaming completions with tight token-budget controls so inline suggestions feel immediate and non-disruptive.

From AE/SE calls: - Wants TTFT p50 < 80ms for single-line completions; ideal p50 ~50-70ms. Emphasized user-perceived latency > average token throughput. 'If the first token shows late, devs abandon the suggestion' (customer quote). - Concerned about jitter (p95 spikes) causing cursor jumps; asks for backpressure strategies. - Cost sensitive at scale; looking for intelligent token budgets per session (default 150 tokens, adaptive growth) and model pinning for reproducibility across releases.

Technical constraints: - VS Code extension streams partial tokens; requires consistent byte-aligned partial flushes. - Must support model version pinning and automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant on Dedicated pools during bursts. - Need K/V prefix caching for common repo headers to reduce repeated context cost. - EU data residency for some customers; Private or Dedicated VPC likely required.

POC ask: 2-week POC embedded in their staging VS Code fleet (~50 internal devs). Goals: TTFT p50 <80ms, jitter p95 <120ms, drop-rate <1%, steady-state throughput 30 reqs/s per shard, average token spend per session <=200 tokens. Measured metrics and dashboard access required.

Buyer signals: Engineering lead committed to pilot; product manager wants integration by end of Q2. Positive reaction to Redwood's optimize recommendations demo (batching + KV caching).

Concise next steps: 1) SE demo + architecture deep-dive (Jonah) 2) Instrumented POC plan and metric dashboard 3) Legal/data residency appendix in SOW.

Quote from last call: 'If you can guarantee TTFT and controlled token budgets we can replace our current provider for IDE completions.'
